# Using Retail Supply Chain Management Software to Improve Your Operations


As a growing retail brand, properly managing your supply chain can feel like an overwhelming, uphill battle. This is often because your current supply chain management (SCM) software is either not purpose-built for retail, or you’re still trying to manage your supply chain the old-fashioned way — with spreadsheets, manual data tracking, and tools that are stretched to fill the gap in your software needs.

Want to test drive the most customizable ERP platform in the market?


If this is your reality, there’s plenty you can do to change direction and start meeting your growth goals — without ripping out the software your ops team relies on.

Why you should consider a retail-native SCM software integration

## Why You Need SCM Software Built for Retail


The market is full of different supply chain management software integrations that are built for a variety of business niches. Some are designed to support complex manufacturing, like automotive production (both consumer and heavy equipment), pharmaceuticals, and healthcare technology. For industries that specialize in logistical support or shipping, they need powerful SCM tools that can help them optimize their routes and shipping speeds.


[Retail has some manufacturing and production workflows](https://www.tailor.tech/resources/posts/importance-of-supply-chain-management-software) , but they’re often far less complicated than manufacturing the parts of an excavator or a passenger vehicle. And larger retail operations might manage their own logistics or have a logistics partner — which means their SCM software needs to be able to interface with the tools their vendors and partners might use.


You might be getting the picture already, but the integration your growing brand chooses needs to be built for retail. But what does that look like?


### Scalable, Flexible, and API-First


In this modern retail environment, you can’t be wasting precious time fighting with rigid workflows and low-compatibility software bundles. Your retail partners, suppliers, and vendors might all be using different software to manage their data, and you don’t want to end up in a situation where you have to haphazardly integrate a new tool just to do business with them. These hurried, emergency integrations are disruptive and expensive to implement.


-


**This is where flexibility really matters.** When you’re unable to move quickly without fires starting, you’re likely too rigid. And if that rushed integration is going to eat up your operating budget and cause disruptions, you’ll be facing the repercussions later. A stack with flexible SCM software wouldn’t cause the same problems.


-


**Is your SCM software scalable?** Scalability is the software’s ability to grow to meet your needs as your own business develops and changes. It’s also the metric that determines how frequently you have to replace that software with another integration.[An SCM integration that’s flexible and scalable will be able to handle everything you can throw at it](https://www.tailor.tech/resources/posts/supply-chain-management-software-features) now, and continue to meet your needs for years to come.


-


**The factor that enables scalability and flexibility.** API-connectivity is the core design choice that promotes both scalability and flexibility in any software integration. With SCM software in particular, this will help it support the numerous lanes of external data it needs to parse, without relying on spreadsheets and manual reconciliation.


## Operational Benefits of Retail Supply Chain Management Software


Next, let’s explore the operational benefits of integrating retail SCM software. The operational impacts fall into three categories:


-


Sync times and data management


-


Partner interfacing


-


Production and logistics efficiency


### Real-Time Sync of Your Most Important Data


One of the first major benefits of having retail supply chain management software is the real-time sync of your logistics, warehousing, vendor, and procurement data. Especially in this modern retail environment, you shouldn’t be making key business decisions based on lagging data reports.


SCM software made for retailers should be able to provide you with as much information about your products, shipments, and materials as quickly as possible.[Waiting for nightly reports](https://www.tailor.tech/resources/posts/erp-reporting) leaves far too large a time gap to properly monitor the state of your operations. When you have retail SCM software built to enable real-time sync, you’ll know where your products are moving, how much inventory exists at each location, and whether or not your suppliers have the materials you need to continue production on time.


### Simplified Vendor, Partner, and Supplier Management


Being able to directly interface with your partners’ data streams to track product sales, pending orders, and outbound fulfillment is essential for operating a modern ecommerce retail brand. Likewise, if your business has a manufacturing or production component, you need to be able to monitor procurement data to ensure you can keep your workflows moving.


[Retail supply chain management software](https://www.tailor.tech/resources/posts/what-supply-chain-management-software-does) can help you generate demand forecasting reports that will simplify the process of choosing which SKUs and product lines to focus on. It also provides you with information about the materials your suppliers or vendors have on hand, and may also provide you with pricing insights to ensure you’re able to get what you need for the cost you want to pay.


Without a modern, retail-focused SCM integration, many of these processes are burdened by spreadsheets, low-information decision-making, and unexpected delays that force you to scramble and disappoint your customers.


### Deeply Integrated Logistics and Production


Another operational benefit to consider is that retail SCM software provides deeper integration into logistics and production workflows. Rather than simply allowing you to track these often complex workflow sets, you can keep them from becoming rigid and inflexible, along with properly managing them.


Without the right SCM software integration, you might find that your insight into your logistics pipeline is hazy at best. You’re subject to getting updates when your third-party warehouses, fulfillment, or bulk product transporters schedule report deliveries. But with a retail SCM software integration that’s API-first, you can gain access to all that data as it’s being updated in their system — removing the wait and cutting out potential for erroneous data.


You can also more dynamically adjust your production processes with better forecasting and real-time market data, which is helped by having more insight into available materials and more accurate sales projections.


## How Composable ERP and SCM Software Work Together to Transform Your Retail Operations


Looking at the feature lists between ERP and SCM software integrations, you might think that you only need one and not the other. Many of the available features overlap, but they functionally cover different needs. SCM software integrations (for the sake of this overview) tend to handle **external data** — or information that’s coming from third parties and retail or warehousing locations you’re not in direct control of.


On the other hand, your ERP manages **internal data** , information, and metrics that originate within software, retail, warehousing, production, and materials sourcing that you directly own or manage. Because each software generally specializes in only half the data you need to operate your business, you need to consider what it would look like to have them work together.


Operational Factors Connected ERP & SCM Software Disconnected ERP & SCM Software


Adaptability and Flexibility High. Composable ERP and SCM software made for retail can respond better to market changes, without missing a beat. Low. Rigid ERP and non-retail SCM software struggle to adapt to market changes and cannot be flexible.


Data Management Comprehensive. You can manage and automatically reconcile data across your entire business, creating a single source of truth. Siloed. Data might be slow to report and be based on fractured authority between different software — resulting in manual reconciliation.


Upgradability Fast, minimal disruption. Improve your existing tools faster, without headaches or breaking processes. Slow, greater disruption risk. Fear upgrading because your system might experience breaking changes.


Scalability High, controlled. Grow your tool’s capacity easily, without worrying about needing to replace them. Low, difficult. Growth is hard to pull off because of rigid structure and workflows that are set in stone.


Software Compatibility Maximized. API-first design allows you to add API-enabled tools easily, with short integration windows. Dependent on architecture. Some ERP and SCM software have decent compatibility, but others don’t. Depending on your combination, your choices may be limited.


Workflows Customizable. Adjust workflows to account for new tools and team use cases. Rigid. Workflows are predetermined by the software and are difficult to change.
